*Updated 2026-10-11 · 119 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and nineteen works. The October 11 sandals piece scores 4 — the first 4 since July 29, ending a run of nineteen weeks at median 2. The last twelve now read 3, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 4, and the sequence matters: the lift came from an object doing double work simultaneously, each sandal pair readable as both the thing placed and the body that wore it. That compression — one object, two legible registers at once — is what separated it from the compositionally resolved but frictionless images that filled the gap.

Camera position has still not moved. Straight-on sits at 27 all-time, overhead at 12, from-behind at 11, low-angle at 4. The recent window shows two overhead frames and nothing else off-axis. Low-angle combined with a misscaled figure has never been attempted as a deliberate pairing across any of the 119 works. The four 4-scored pieces in the archive each generated friction between a body and a mismatched object, but none got there through the camera position itself creating that mismatch as a physical optical consequence. That combination is still the most actionable single variable untouched.

Figure count is marginally more active. The recent window shows two frames with two or more figures, one with none — slightly more populated than the previous cycle, but the surgical trolley piece confirms that a second figure placed without structural opposition adds count without adding pressure. The October 11 piece scored 4 with no figures at all, which is the cleaner lesson: the object can carry the full weight when it is doing two things at once.

Registers have tightened again. Aftermath leads the recent window at 3 of 12, menace and suspension at 2 each, defiance at 2. Reckoning has not appeared since July. Reprieve since July. Impotence appeared once across the entire archive. Exhaustion twice, not since June. These are not exhausted — they simply haven't been attempted when the anchor warranted them.

The work is technically disciplined and has just demonstrated it can still break its own plateau; the question is whether the camera moves before the next long flatline sets in.
